goal.en: Know when a ready-made phrase is doing work and when it is standing in for thought.
goal.ar: أن تعرف متى تؤدي العبارة الجاهزة عملاً، ومتى تحلّ محلّ التفكير.

text.en: Most idioms began as pictures and stopped being seen. Nobody visualises a table when they “table a motion”. A dead metaphor is not a fault — it is simply vocabulary now.
text.ar: بدأت أغلب التعبيرات الاصطلاحية صوراً ثم كفّ الناس عن رؤيتها. فلا أحد يتخيّل طاولةً حين يقول table a motion. والاستعارة الميتة ليست عيباً، بل صارت مفردةً لا أكثر.

head: Phrase
Original picture
Now
rows: a line prisoners could not cross

text.en: The danger is the half-alive metaphor: alive enough to clash with the next one, dead enough that the writer never noticed.
text.ar: الخطر في الاستعارة نصف الحية: حيةٌ بما يكفي لتصطدم بما بعدها، وميتةٌ بما يكفي ألّا ينتبه الكاتب.

head: Mixed
Why it fails
rows: We must nip it in the bud before it snowballs.
Let's not put the cart before the horse until we've tested the water.
This opens a can of worms that we'll have to iron out.
He's a loose cannon we need to rein in.

text.en: Test any idiom by picturing it literally. If the picture is absurd or fights the next one, the reader will see it even if you did not.
text.ar: اختبر أي تعبير بتخيّله حرفياً. فإن كانت الصورة عبثية أو تصادم ما بعدها فسيراها القارئ وإن غابت عنك.

text.en: Mixed metaphors are funny, and being accidentally funny in a serious document costs you the reader's confidence for the next paragraph.
text.ar: خلط الاستعارات مضحك، والإضحاك غير المقصود في وثيقة جادّة يكلّفك ثقة القارئ في الفقرة التالية.

title.en: When a cliché is the right choice

text.en: Originality is not always a virtue. In a safety notice, a legal clause or a condolence message, the familiar phrase is understood instantly and carries no ego with it.
text.ar: الأصالة ليست فضيلةً دائماً. ففي لافتة سلامة أو بند قانوني أو رسالة تعزية تُفهم العبارة المألوفة فوراً ولا تحمل معها أنا الكاتب.

text.en: The cliché to avoid is the one that replaces a fact: “passionate about excellence” and “results-driven team player” say nothing a reader can check.
text.ar: المبتذل الذي يجب تجنّبه هو ما يحلّ محلّ الواقعة: فعبارات مثل passionate about excellence وresults-driven team player لا تقول شيئاً يستطيع القارئ التحقق منه.

prompt.en: Why is “grasp an idea” not a problem in serious writing?
prompt.ar: لماذا لا تُعدّ عبارة grasp an idea مشكلة في الكتابة الجادّة؟

options: The metaphor is dead, so no picture is triggered.
The metaphor is fresh, so it catches attention.
It only appears in spoken English, never written.
It is a technical term with a precise meaning.

explanation.en: Nobody sees a hand. Dead metaphors have become ordinary vocabulary and cause no clash.
explanation.ar: لا أحد يرى يداً هنا. فالاستعارات الميتة صارت مفردات عادية ولا تُحدث تصادماً.

prompt.en: Which phrase is a half-alive metaphor, still able to clash?
prompt.ar: أي عبارة استعارة نصف حية لا تزال قادرة على التصادم؟

options: the tip of the iceberg
to run out of time
to grasp an idea
to meet a deadline

explanation.en: The iceberg is still visible, so what follows it must not melt, sink or catch fire.
explanation.ar: جبل الجليد ما زال مرئياً، فما يليه يجب ألّا يذوب أو يغرق أو يشتعل.

prompt.en: Match the phrase with the picture it came from.
prompt.ar: صِل العبارة بالصورة التي جاءت منها.

pairs: a line prisoners could not cross

explanation.en: Knowing the picture tells you how alive the metaphor still is, and therefore how carefully to handle it.
explanation.ar: معرفة الصورة تخبرك بمقدار ما بقي من حياة الاستعارة، ومن ثمّ بمقدار الحذر اللازم.

options: We must nip this in the bud before it snowballs.
We must deal with this before it grows any further.
We must stop this before it becomes a real problem.
We must act now rather than wait for it to spread.

explanation.en: A bud belongs to a plant; a snowball rolls downhill. The reader sees both and neither survives.
explanation.ar: البرعم من النبات، وكرة الثلج تتدحرج، فيرى القارئ الصورتين ولا تنجو واحدة منهما.

prompt.en: Which sentence produces an absurd picture?

options: This opens a can of worms that we will have to iron out.
This raises questions that we will have to resolve.
This creates complications we will need to work through.
This uncovers problems that will take time to settle.

explanation.en: Worms cannot be ironed. Two idioms, each fine alone, destroy each other here.
explanation.ar: لا تُكوى الديدان. تعبيران كلٌّ منهما سليم منفرداً، ويُفسد أحدهما الآخر هنا.

prompt.en: How do you test an idiom before using it?
prompt.ar: كيف تختبر تعبيراً اصطلاحياً قبل استعماله؟

options: Picture it literally and see whether the image holds.
Count how many words the whole phrase contains.
Check whether it appears in a dictionary at all.
Replace it with a longer and more formal phrase.

explanation.en: The literal picture is exactly what a reader half-sees, which is why clashes are noticed.
explanation.ar: الصورة الحرفية هي ما يراه القارئ نصف رؤية، ولذلك تُلاحظ التصادمات.

prompt.en: Which sentence has a mixed metaphor?

options: He is a loose cannon and we need to rein him in.
He is unpredictable and we need to control him.
He is a loose cannon and we need to watch him.
He acts without warning and needs closer supervision.

explanation.en: Cannons have no reins. The third keeps the cannon and drops the horse, which is why it survives.
explanation.ar: المدافع لا أعنّة لها. والجملة الثالثة تُبقي المدفع وتُسقط الحصان، ولهذا تنجو.

prompt.en: Where is a conventional phrase the better choice?
prompt.ar: أين تكون العبارة التقليدية هي الخيار الأفضل؟

options: A message of condolence to a colleague.
The opening line of a magazine feature.
A description of your own work in an application.
A slogan for a new product launch.

explanation.en: Condolence is not the place for originality; the familiar words carry no ego and are understood instantly.
explanation.ar: ليست التعزية موضع أصالة، فالعبارات المألوفة لا تحمل أنا الكاتب وتُفهم فوراً.

prompt.en: Which line belongs in a job application?

options: I rebuilt the reporting process and cut month-end from nine days to three.
I am passionate about excellence and driven by outstanding results.
I am a results-driven team player with a can-do attitude to work.
I always go the extra mile and think outside the box every day.

explanation.en: One checkable fact beats four stock phrases. The clichés here are not ugly; they are empty.
explanation.ar: واقعة واحدة قابلة للتحقق تتفوق على أربع عبارات جاهزة. والمبتذل هنا ليس قبيحاً بل فارغاً.

prompt.en: Which kind of cliché is the one to eliminate?
prompt.ar: أي نوع من المبتذل هو الذي يجب حذفه؟

options: The one that replaces a fact the reader could check.
The one that has been in the language for centuries.
The one that began life as a visual metaphor.
The one that appears in more than one language.

explanation.en: Age is not the problem. Emptiness is: “passionate about excellence” cannot be true or false.
explanation.ar: القِدم ليس المشكلة بل الخواء: فعبارة passionate about excellence لا تحتمل صدقاً ولا كذباً.

prompt.en: Which sentence opens a feature article most freshly?
prompt.ar: أي جملة تفتتح مقالاً صحفياً بأكثر طزاجة؟

options: The bakery has been closing at noon for forty years, and nobody has asked why.
Since time immemorial, bakeries have played a vital role in our communities.
At the end of the day, a bakery is the beating heart of any neighbourhood.
It goes without saying that bakeries are an important part of local life.

explanation.en: A specific oddity earns attention. The others reach for phrases the reader has skimmed a thousand times.
explanation.ar: الغرابة المحددة تكسب الانتباه، أما البقية فتلجأ إلى عبارات مرّ عليها القارئ ألف مرة.

prompt.en: Why does “the tip of the iceberg that we must nip in the bud” fail?
prompt.ar: لماذا تفشل عبارة the tip of the iceberg that we must nip in the bud؟

options: Both metaphors are alive enough to be seen at once.
Both metaphors are completely dead and invisible.
The sentence contains a grammatical error as well.
Icebergs and buds are both associated with cold.

explanation.en: If both pictures are visible, the reader sees a gardener pruning an iceberg.
explanation.ar: إذا كانت الصورتان مرئيتين رأى القارئ بستانياً يقلّم جبل جليد.

prompt.en: Fix the mixture in one word: “We must nip this in the bud before it ___ .” (something a plant can do)
prompt.ar: أصلح الخلط بكلمة واحدة مما يفعله النبات: We must nip this in the bud before it ___

explanation.en: Keep one picture and let it finish. Growing, spreading and taking root all belong to the plant.
explanation.ar: أبقِ صورة واحدة ودعها تكتمل، فالنمو والانتشار والتجذّر كلها من عالم النبات.

prompt.en: A safety notice needs a warning about wet floors. What is right?
prompt.ar: تحتاج لافتة سلامة تحذيراً من الأرضية المبللة. ما الصواب؟

options: Caution: wet floor.
Beware: slippery slope.
Danger lurks below.
Tread very carefully.

explanation.en: The conventional phrase is read at a glance. Originality here costs seconds a reader may not have.
explanation.ar: العبارة التقليدية تُقرأ بلمحة، والأصالة هنا تكلّف ثوانٍ قد لا يملكها القارئ.

prompt.en: A report says the team is “committed to delivering value”. What have you learned?
prompt.ar: قال تقرير إن الفريق committed to delivering value. ماذا عرفت؟

options: Nothing that could be confirmed or contradicted.
That the team met its targets for the year.
That the team has changed its priorities.
That the team is smaller than it once was.

explanation.en: No team ever claims the opposite, which is how you know the sentence carries no information.
explanation.ar: لا فريق يدّعي العكس، وبهذا تعرف أن الجملة لا تحمل معلومة.
